Electrocardiogram During Tachycardia    Image Description: Shows P waves upright in leads II, III, and aVF with sinus rate of 96 beats per minute. Grouped beating pattern with 1 P wave producing 2 QRS complexes, creating a regularly irregular rhythm.
Prior Imaging:    Transesophageal echocardiography revealed pulmonic valve vegetations and severe tricuspid valve regurgitation secondary to a flail leaflet.

bindings.label: Patient presented to emergency department with severe back pain, light-headedness, and chest pain
Medical history includes infective endocarditis and hepatitis C secondary to ongoing intravenous drug use
Recently underwent tricuspid valve replacement with a 29-mm bioprosthetic Carpentier-Edwards valve, complicated by transient third-degree heart block; two days after pacemaker placement
Physical exam showed blood pressure 94/60 mm Hg and heart rate 150-190 beats per minute
Transesophageal echocardiography reveals pulmonic valve vegetations and severe tricuspid regurgitation due to a flail leaflet
ECG shows grouped beating with 1:2 AV conduction, suggesting a conduction abnormality
Blood cultures and inflammatory markers remain unavailable
Pacemaker lead vegetations and pericardial effusion were not assessed on transesophageal echocardiography
